corpus_item: RI-MAG06 §B — the consuming-system map. Every row below is a system a spell moves.
note: The W1-14 round-1 verdict measured `open` doing 31 hp OF DAMAGE TO A CREATURE, because there
was no lock in the build for it to open. A verb with no object is not a verb. This file is
the object set: the locks, wards, breakables, repairables, keys and shrines the Warding and
Root-Speech utility half of the catalogue acts on, placed at real world coordinates in the
arenas and cells the harness can reach.
It is DATA, not a quest. `magic-utility.json` under game/data/quests/ is what turns these
objects into resolutions; this file only says they exist and what state they are in. The
durable half of every mutation here is written through to sim.world.doors_unlocked /
shortcuts_opened, which are already on the save manifest — a door a spell opened stays open
across a save, and a critic can see it in the save rather than only in a probe.

locks.prose: A collar of black lacquer set into swamp-oak, three wards deep.
A strongbox with a Rootkeeper seal, still wet.
A grate whose collar has rusted almost through.
Four wards. Nobody picks this; you either have the key or you have Warding.
The sluice-gate collar. Five wards, and the fifth is not a ward at all.

traps.prose: A bead of sap on the threshold, holding a tension it should not have.
A needle behind the lip of the lid.
The board under the sluice sits a finger too high.

breakables.prose: Brick gone soft with a century of standing water.
A knot of hist-root grown across the gallery mouth.
A stone lid, cracked once already.

items.prose: Two picks left with any spring in them.
Past mending. RI-MAG06 §B: mend_item refuses below 10%.

keys.prose: On a hook behind the counter, where nobody looks.
In the silt under the third piling.
